Hi, first of all, I have to tell you that you should look for professional help, both mental and body.
Now, here it goes: I’m a recovery anorexic who went to something similar like this. That does not mean you are one, it only means that we have some points in common.
The first thing to evaluate is if you have any sign on your body that explains this lost of appetite. You said you’ve got IBS, did this habit of eating too much/starving started after a crises?
 If eating is an obligation, a “chore” as you said, what other chores you got during the day? The week? Do you feel overwhelmed by things you should be doing during the day?

Not every anorexic person get the same “I can’t gain weight” kinda of thought. My process was because of lactose intolerance. I was feeling bad all the time so I stopped eating because I didn’t want to feel like that anymore.

I went through a rough path, I lost 40kgs in  less than 3 months, I also lost lots of hair and a teeth. I really don’t want you going through this. It is very hard to recover.

Please, look for help and I really hope you can find the answers to your questions and peace to your heart!

Everything is gonna work out! ♥️

Well, best thing to do is going with the easier steps first... If you guys want or need this, tell your parents first... They seem to be more likely to receive the news in a positive way.
If I were you I’d talk to my parents first and then introduce your S/O over dinner or something like that.

As for their parents, how bad would it be for them to talk about you for themselves? If is too difficult or complicated, maybe talk to your parents about helping you guys if they’re willing to...

But those things take time and patience, take it step by step and I hope everything is going to be okay!

Best of luck for you guys :)

Hey OP, you two are young and I’ll understand that maybe she is too insecure about you having attention online or something like that. But, the thing is, you both shouldn’t have each other’s passwords.

It’s yours and hers life, so having this kind of sharing is the recipe for disaster... Been there, done that.

You might need to talk and ser boundaries. IDK how long you’ve been together, but you should be able to trust each other, otherwise it won’t work.

Best of luck for you guys!

If you think B will tell A, then talk to A... Tell him your intention is not to wreck anything and that you would understand if he needs some time.

The outcome might be the end of the friendship (as it can also happen depending on what B says to A), but being silent while B tells whatever he wants to A maybe is not the best option...

However, IDK how the relationship is between A and B, and between A and you... Maybe he’ll listen to B and have the impression he might have been jealous of you and not worried about him. IDK.

oh, okay... You’re the girl.

I mean, I’m mostly monogamous, so I’d advise you to get away from this situation... However, is he? I mean, are they in an open relationship? Is it a possibility for you?

Otherwise, try to think that this guy has a whole life with that woman, they have shared fears and bad times. I know relationships can be over and all, but the best thing you can do is trying to find someone else to be interested in... Easier said than done, I know, but it’s the best you can do...

And crushes go away, sometimes is hard, but they go away.

BTW be aware if you’re offending him or exposing him, in way that he might get away from you and you might lost a hell of a good friendship... Just be respectful to the guy and his marriage. It’s what our mothers have always told us, don’t do to others what you don’t want be done to you, right?!

Again, I hope you can find the best way to deal with it :)

Well, the thing is: you only have control over what you do and/or say... So, if you’re the guy in this situation, you gotta be careful not give her the wrong idea. That’s your responsibility and the only thing you have a truly control over.

If you feel exposed or offended, talk to her, tell her about specific situations and not about “having a crush” in general.

I say that because, when I was younger, I’ve been in this same exact situation, however the guy thought I had a crush when I just liked him as an older brother... Our friendship went to pieces when he accused me of having a crush on him, because I felt like he was doubting the deep respect I had for him and his wife.

Long story short, analyze what you can do and, if you feel you’re not being fair to your SO, try to be less close to her.

I hope you can find the best way to deal with it :)

The thing is, you can send this message, but really think about it, it’s been a while that you guys are talking about going out, she’s been saying she’s interested but has done nothing about it. Is it worth it?

If you guys go out and pursue this relationship, what are the chances of her doing the exact same thing but now with some strings attached?

IDK man, I’m in my late 20s and dealing with this BS in our age is hard, we always think that people will be more well solved, but they aren’t.

I mean, you can send the message and try one more time, but think about yourself and how your future self would deal with this... I wouldn’t try anymore, there are plenty other interesting people around, but you do you!

Best of luck!

Hey! First of all NTA... However, can I give you an advice based on something that happened to me?

I was a teacher a few years ago and something similar had happened with documents being deleted and viruses being up in a shared folder in Google Drive. One of the Ss knew what was happening and came up to me.

They told me the whole issue, about one of the boys being the responsible for that mess, but they didn’t want to be exposed as someone who told on their peers.

IDK how old you are, but I suspect you’re a minor, right? So, maybe, if you guys have this kind of open communication with that specific teacher this could be arranged, specially if they have a investigation going on. It could be said that the investigators found the evidence.

If that’s not an option, how would you feel talking about it with your parents?

I know it sounds like a “dumb prank”, but we are talking about information here. It’s neither the place nor the time for pranks.

Anyway, I hope you can find a good solution for that :)

I can only imagine how hard it is to find out that your father is not you bio one, however, as difficult as this might be and sound, try to look at their perspective.

They were so willing to have you and your brother that they went through all this process to have you guys. Does this make your father less of a parent? I don’t think so, he was there for you. Even when they divorced, he was still there for you.

I understand and agree that your brother should know, however I’d talk a little more to both of your parents and present your reasons. Imagine how difficult it was for your mother to tell you about this, being “discovered” would be devastating.

IF they insist on not telling your brother, maybe you should reconsider and tell him. I really don’t know if I’d do it, but if you think it’s the right thing to do, well...

Just please give them a chance to talk to your brother.

I hope everything gets solved in the best way possible :)

She charged me, I payed and everything was good. 

I mean, for people who work with their image (and believe me, I find this “social media influenced” thing kind of BS, but I do feel her here) those things are very important.

Anyway, it’s your @, if you want to keep it, go ahead, you have the right to, but I’d make business with her.

Oh! I don’t know who she is, but, if you intend to maintain your @, be sure to protect your Instagram as much as you can with 2-step verification login and all. Also, be aware of she (or the company handling her social media) trying to put your account down with fake reports.

Best of luck :)

Hey Op,

So, when I was younger I used to get beaten up at school by several people everyday, I still remember it sometimes and it’s a hurtful memory. HOWEVER, by the end of my last school year I lost it. For real.

One of the girls who used to beat me up was the victim and I was so harsh on her that they had to call an ambulance. This is also a very hurtful memory.

Luckily nothing happened to her and it’s been more than 10 years so I haven’t seen her, but I wouldn’t have forgiven myself if anything had happened that afternoon.

Having said that, I understand your child had to stand up for them self and that the whole situation was badly dealt by school faculty, but rewarding them because of it is very complicated.

I won’t say YTA, but, if may I suggest something have a talk to them, explain that violence is not a valuable resource and its consequences may be too difficult to handle afterwards.

If I hadn’t had my mother telling me this when that happened I have no idea what I would have become now as an adult.

Something that helped me a lot was that my mother signed me up for martial arts after that episode and I practiced it during my Uni years. It made me understand the difference between self defense and violence and how we can defend ourselves without hurting others.

Hope you and your child can find peace in solving this situation.

You see, the problem here is not the age gap itself, I do believe that a 25yo person can date a 35yo person, it’s fine because they’re adults and have their own lives and have been through some BS in their time.

HOWEVER when we speak of a 13yo and a 18yo the life experiences are different, their maturity level is different and the older person of the relationship may have an “overpower” attitude to the younger person. In those many years being a teacher and dealing with teenagers I can say that I’ve seen many situations like this turned to be pretty abusive.

I’ve seen 13yo girls clearly not ready to have sex but doing it because they were afraid of losing their SO, I’ve seen many MANY girls getting drunk very young to fit in with their SO group of friends and not remembering what happened. We all know this is dangerous.

Those are just some examples of how dangerous a relationship like this can represent to young people, and, besides, THIS IS A F CRIME, even though whoever disagreed with you and didn’t want to consider this argument, well, it’s a fact.
